chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Hammad, from one who heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Beware of asking people (for what they have), for it is a humiliation in the world, and a poverty that you hasten, and a lengthy reckoning on the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: Day of Resurrection / Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and worldly consequences of begging according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who links the spiritual dignity of the believer to self-sufficiency, warning that begging induces immediate humiliation and accelerates worldly poverty. The Imam further emphasizes the eschatological consequence, noting that such acts incur a prolonged accounting on the Day of Judgment, reflecting the Shia emphasis on preserving one's honor before God and the community.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Hammad, 
(It has been narrated) from the one who heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying:
‘Beware of begging the people, for it is a humiliation in the world and poverty which you are hastening, and a lengthy Reckoning on the Day of Judgement’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Husayn ibn Hammad from the one who had heard abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Never beg people for financial help; it is humiliation in this world, a poverty that you make it to approach you quickly and on the Day of Judgment presentation of accounts for it will keep you much longer.’”
